# Fixtures

Every file here is **synthetic**: the record shapes, keys, markers and ordering mirror what the hosts write, and every piece of text, name, path and id is invented. Nothing was copied from anyone's real transcripts, hook payloads or accounts. The invented developer is "sam"; the invented projects are `billing-api`, `web-app`, `ledger-cli` and a few others under `/home/sam/projects`.

The formats they mirror (see `docs/hosts.md`):

| Fixture | Mirrors |
|---|---|
| `claude-lines.json` | one Claude Code transcript line per case, as written by Claude Code 2.1.170 to 2.1.289: typed turn, mid-turn `queued_command` attachment, legacy typed turn without `origin`, tool result, task notification, queued task notification, skill/meta record, sub-agent sidechain record, a `claude -p` prompt (`sdk-cli`), a prompt with `turnOrigin: "sdk"`, a `queue-operation` record |
| `tail-lines.json` | the lines the prompt-time situation reads from a live transcript's tail: Claude assistant text and tool_use records, a tool result, a typed turn; Codex `AgentMessage`, `UserMessage` and `CommandExecution` events (Claude Code 2.1.289, Codex 0.160) |
| `codex/sessions/...` | Codex rollouts (Codex Desktop 0.147, `codex exec` 0.160): an interactive session with `session_meta`, polluted `response_item` user copies and `UserMessage` events (including a bare skill invocation), an `exec` rollout and a sub-agent rollout (both must be skipped) |
| `code/sessions/...` | an Every Code rollout (`code_cli_rs`, source `cli`; no `UserMessage` events, `response_item` user turns plus a `== System Status ==` automatic message) |
| `show/*.jsonl` | three transcript windows for `recall show` (`test/show.test.mjs`): a Claude Code window (30 lines: an assistant reply, the stop-hook summary, queued task notifications, the typed statement at line 15, its attachments, a file-history snapshot, thinking, a `Workflow` tool call and result, session metadata records), a Codex rollout window (51 lines: exec calls with token records, reasoning items, `CommandExecution` events, the statement as a `response_item` and a `UserMessage` event at lines 33 and 34, assistant messages written twice, a `spawn_agent` function call) and a second Codex window that the test stores as `.jsonl.zst` (53 lines, statement at line 22; the test compresses it with zstd). The tests splice the harness lines of `claude-lines.json` into the Claude window to show they are not conversation; that sequence is spliced, not a conversation |
| `hook-inputs/*.json` | hook stdin payloads of Claude Code 2.1.287 and Codex 0.160 (`UserPromptSubmit`, and the `Stop` payloads that the plugin must now refuse) |
| `headless/` | the evidence that tells a person from an automated worker: hook stdin payloads and the relevant hook-process environment of a nested `claude -p`, an attended session, `codex exec`, an interactive Codex TUI session, Codex's internal memory agent; the user record a nested `claude -p` writes; line 1 (`session_meta`) of an exec, a TUI and a `security_scan` rollout |
| `compaction/` | compaction markers and the owner lines around them: Claude `compact_boundary` (with `preservedMessages`) and `isCompactSummary` records, Codex `compacted` records with `replacement_history`, the typed lines that the tests splice into short sequences. They do not claim the spliced sequences were conversations |
| `roster.sample.json`, `usage-json.sample.json` | an invented roster (twelve homes, five of them eligible for work) and invented `usage --json` output for it |
| `history/codex-history.jsonl`, `history/claude-history.jsonl` | typed-prompt logs (`<home>/history.jsonl`): Codex / Every Code rows `{session_id, ts, text}` (slash commands, a bare command, a row with another person's address) and Claude Code rows `{display, pastedContents, timestamp, project, sessionId}` (a paste placeholder with its text, the same sentence in two projects, a temp-directory project, an older row without `sessionId`) |
| `codex-legacy/rollout-*.jsonl` | two Codex rollouts from before `session_meta` (Codex CLI of mid 2025): a bare header line, `record_type` markers, bare response items without timestamps (an environment-context turn, typed turns, reasoning, a `shell` call and its output, an assistant reply); one session is named by a typed-prompt log in the tests, the other is a program's brief |
| `desktop-envelopes.json` | turns as the desktop apps send them: the Codex app's context sections (attached files and applications, in-app browser state and its `<in-app-browser-context>` block, selections, response annotations, review findings, browser and diff comments) ahead of `## My request for Codex:` or `## My request:`, and Claude desktop quote replies (`<!-- reply -->`, `<!-- reply 2 -->`, `<!-- attach -->` with `>` quoted lines), each with the words the filter must keep |

Large fields (`base_instructions`, tool output, summaries, plugin lists) are replaced by short invented text ending in `[...elided for fixture]`. Ids are well-formed but invented (UUID versions kept: v4 for Claude, v7 for Codex), timestamps are plausible, versions are real host versions.

Tests derive expectations from the fixtures' own fields where they can and otherwise assert on the invented text, so changing an invented sentence means changing the assertion next to it.

To check that no test file shares text, a millisecond timestamp or a session id with a real history, run `RECALL_PRIVACY_STATEMENTS=/path/to/statements.jsonl npm test` (`test/fixtures-privacy.test.mjs`; skipped when the variable is unset).
